abstract: |
  This memo specifies the repositioning of the paper formerly titled "Liquidity, Activism
  Disclosure, and Takeover Premia" (draft_v2) for submission to a top finance journal. The new
  framing: the Schedule 13D disclosure rule is the revelation technology of the market for
  corporate control. The theory core is simplified to a three-branch model with a provable
  headline theorem (disclosure attenuation), an honest endpoint-plus-region treatment of the
  liquidity hump, and a committed empirical section built on the SEC's February 5, 2024
  acceleration of the 13D filing window. Target: JF/RFS; alternative JFE.
---

# The Angle {#sec-angle}

## The repositioning in one paragraph

Move from *"a static microstructure model of the exit–voice margin with numerically verified
comparative statics"* to **"the 13D disclosure rule as the revelation technology of the market
for corporate control."** The model's disclosed/inferred inference partition is the first
formalization of *how the market learns about activism-driven control events* — precisely the
gap that Back, Collin-Dufresne, Fos, Li and Ljungqvist (2018, *Econometrica*) and Burkart and
Lee (2022, *RFS*) explicitly leave to future work. Nobody — not Ordóñez-Calafi and Bernhardt
(2022), Cetemen et al. (2026), Albuquerque–Fos–Schroth (2022), Johnson–Swem (2021), or
Celentano–Levine (2025) — links market liquidity or the disclosure rule to takeover premia,
theoretically or structurally.

## Why this angle wins

1. **The gap is quotable.** Back et al. (2018) assume a fixed disclosure horizon and call
   endogenizing the 5%-threshold timing future work; Burkart and Lee (2022) "do not endogenize
   the acquisition of the toehold in anonymous, predisclosure markets" and leave the
   pre-/post-disclosure interaction open. We occupy both gaps at once.
2. **Frontier taste.** Every top-3 theory paper in this space, 2022–2026 (Burkart–Lee RFS 2022;
   Levit–Malenko–Maug JF 2024 and JF 2026; Kakhbod et al. RFS 2023; Chen–Gupta–Starmans JFE
   2026), is fully analytical, one-mechanism-elegant, institutionally anchored, and closes with
   a measurement section. A numerically verified headline result has no precedent; a Brouwer
   existence argument plus honestly labeled numerical uniqueness is acceptable *if the headline
   comparative statics are proved*.
3. **The policy hook is live and unclaimed.** The SEC's Modernization of Beneficial Ownership
   Reporting (Rel. 33-11253; adopted October 10, 2023; compliance **February 5, 2024**) shortened
   the initial 13D window from 10 calendar days to 5 business days. No published or SSRN-visible
   empirical work exploits it yet; one working paper engages the window trade-off theoretically.
   The window is open but closing.
4. **Differentiation from the most dangerous competitor.** Celentano and Levine (2025, R&R at
   RFS) estimate activism's equilibrium effect on M&A with no trading, no price formation, and a
   stake fixed at the 5% statutory threshold. One sentence on page 1: *they take prices and
   liquidity as given; we make liquidity and the disclosure rule the state variables, and the
   takeover premium an equilibrium object of order-flow inference and tender free-riding.*

## Framing device

Following Bond, Edmans and Goldstein (2012) and Goldstein (2023), the paper studies
**revelatory** price efficiency (RPE) — what the price reveals to a specific decision-maker, the
bidder — rather than forecasting efficiency. A disclosure *rule* is a policy lever on RPE.
Goldstein (2023) lists RPE-oriented empirics and feedback interacting with corporate-control
frictions as open problems; this paper answers both.

# The Simplified Model {#sec-model}

## Players, timing, and information

All players are risk neutral. There is one blockholder ($B$), one noise trader, one competitive
market maker ($M$), and one potential bidder.

- **$t=0$.** Nature draws firm value $v \sim \mathcal{N}(\mu_v, \sigma_v^2)$. The blockholder
  privately observes $s = v + \varepsilon$, $\varepsilon \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma_\varepsilon^2)$,
  and holds an initial stake normalized to one share.
- **$t=1$ (trade and disclose).** The blockholder chooses an action $(q, a)$ from the
  three-branch menu
  $$
  (q, a) \in \{ \underbrace{(-1, 0)}_{\text{Exit}},\; \underbrace{(0, 1)}_{\text{Quiet}},\;
  \underbrace{(+1, 1)}_{\text{Public}} \},
  $$
  where $q$ is the order and $a \in \{0,1\}$ engagement. (The four-branch menu of draft_v2 is
  pruned: Hold folds into the trading decision; it collapses at baseline anyway.) Noise demand
  $z \in \{-1, 0, +1\}$ with
  $$
  \Pr(z = 0) = 1 - \kappa, \qquad \Pr(z = +1) = \Pr(z = -1) = \tfrac{\kappa}{2},
  $$
  so $\kappa \in [0,1]$ is the liquidity/noise intensity. The market maker observes total order
  flow $X = q + z \in \{-2, \dots, +2\}$ and the disclosure flag $D = \mathbf{1}\{q = +1\}$, and
  sets
  $$
  P(X, D) = \delta\, \mathbb{E}[Y \mid X, D],
  $$
  with $\delta$ a normalization (unit share mass, $\delta = 1$ in the baseline).
- **$t=1.5$ (bidder entry).** The bidder observes $(P, D)$ and a private synergy shock
  $\xi \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma_\xi^2)$, and enters iff
  $$
  \Pi_B = \bar{S} - P + \xi - \bar{m}(X, D) - K \;\geq\; 0,
  $$
  so the entry probability is
  $$
  p(P, D) = \Phi\!\left( \frac{\bar{S} - P - \bar{m}(X, D) - K}{\sigma_\xi} \right),
  \qquad \frac{\partial p}{\partial P} < 0
  \quad \text{(bid monotonicity, proved)}.
  $$
- **$t=2$ (payoffs).** If a bid occurs, $Y = P + m^R(a)$; otherwise $Y = v + a\tilde{\Delta}$.
  The premium wedge $m_1 > m_0$ is microfounded in the appendix tender game (D7): with
  free-rider floor $\varphi$, entry probability $q$, and dilution $\psi$,
  $$
  \lambda \;=\; 1 - q\,(1 - \gamma)\,\psi \;\in\; [0, 1] \quad \text{(proved, closed form)}.
  $$

## Disclosure strictness as a model primitive

The key architectural change from draft_v2: disclosure strictness is now an explicit parameter
$\tau$, not a narrative. A stricter regime (lower threshold, shorter window) shifts ex-ante mass
from the inferred branch to the disclosed branch:
$$
\omega_P = \omega_P(\tau), \qquad \omega_P'(\tau) > 0,
$$
and the window length maps to inferred-branch noise through the Back et al. (2018) isomorphism
$T \leftrightarrow \sigma^2 T$. This is what turns the disclosure result into a policy
comparative static — the 10-to-5-day acceleration and the 5%-vs-3% cross-country contrast are
both movements in $\tau$.

## Equilibrium

A perfect Bayesian equilibrium consists of (i) a weakly ordered cutoff strategy
$k_1 \leq k_0 \leq k_D$ over the signal $s$; (ii) Bayes-consistent posteriors
$\pi(X, D) = \Pr(a = 1 \mid X, D)$; (iii) the bidder's entry rule; (iv) the competitive price
fixed point $P = \mathbb{E}[Y \mid X, D]$. Existence follows from Brouwer's theorem on the
cutoff polytope $\Theta$ (proved, unconditional under (A1), (A2), (A4)). Uniqueness is stated as
a labeled numerical regularity (multistart convergence), never as a theorem — the EGJ (2015)
posture of region-wise characterization rather than global uniqueness claims.

# Main Results and Proof Plan {#sec-results}

## Proved objects already in hand

The posterior block is closed form: the disclosed branch is degenerate, $\pi(X, 1) = 1$, and
$\kappa$-invariant (proved); the inferred branch satisfies $\pi(-2, 0) = 0$ with $\pi(X, 0)$
rational in $(\omega, \kappa)$ (proved). Bid monotonicity, the dominance lemma pruning the
action menu, and existence are proved. Endpoint symmetry is proved:
$$
\Delta^{\min}(0^{+}) \;=\; \Delta^{\min}(1^{-}),
$$
because at both liquidity limits the $D = 0$ posterior law converges to the same two-point
distribution $\{0, \bar{\pi}\}$.

## T2 — Disclosure attenuation (the headline theorem)

At fixed cutoffs, the expected activism premium decomposes across the two branches as
$$
\Delta^{\mathrm{act}}(\kappa; \tau)
\;=\;
(\tilde{m} - m_0)\Big[ \omega_P(\tau)\, \bar{p}_1
\;+\; \big(1 - \omega_P(\tau)\big)\, \mathbb{E}_{D=0}\, h(\kappa) \Big],
$$
where $\bar{p}_1$ is the disclosed-branch bid incidence ($\kappa$-invariant) and
$\mathbb{E}_{D=0} h(\kappa)$ carries all inference sensitivity. Since the disclosed component is
$\kappa$-free, the liquidity sensitivity satisfies
$$
\left| \frac{\partial \Delta^{\mathrm{act}}}{\partial \kappa} \right|
\;=\;
(\tilde{m} - m_0)\,\big(1 - \omega_P(\tau)\big)\,
\left| \frac{\partial}{\partial \kappa} \mathbb{E}_{D=0}\, h(\kappa) \right|,
$$
which is **strictly decreasing in $\tau$** whenever $\omega_P'(\tau) > 0$ and the inferred-branch
term is non-degenerate. The cross-partial sign is one line given the proved $\kappa$-invariance
of the disclosed branch. **Theorem T2 (general equilibrium, region version):** reusing the D8
inversion-free bound
$$
\left\| \frac{dk}{d\kappa} \right\| \;\leq\; \frac{\| \partial_\kappa T \|}{1 - L},
\qquad L \leq 0.836 \text{ at baseline},
$$
the attenuation sign is certified on a checkable region of primitives, exactly parallel to the
D8 region theorem. We do not chase a global GE sign — the D8 counterexample logic warns against
it, and the region statement is the honest, publishable form.

## T4 — The liquidity hump, honestly stated

The hump is **not** the headline. It is presented as three objects, in descending order of
strength:

1. **Endpoint symmetry (proved):** $\Delta^{\min}(0^{+}) = \Delta^{\min}(1^{-})$.
2. **Certified region (computed, machine-checked):** strict single-peakedness of
   $\Delta^{\min}(\kappa)$ is certified on $\kappa \in [0.35, 0.825]$ under the checkable
   conditions (R1) pointwise dominance and (R2) integral control (D8). Channel (A) is
   single-peaked at fixed cutoffs iff the chord condition
   $$
   \mathcal{C}(\bar{\pi}) \;=\; h(0) - 2 h\!\left(\tfrac{\bar{\pi}}{2}\right) + h(\bar{\pi}) \;<\; 0,
   \qquad h = \pi \cdot p,
   $$
   holds (proved, conditional on $(\mathcal{C}^*)$).
3. **Falsifiable prediction (numerical elsewhere):** the interior peak $\kappa^\dagger \approx
   0.59$ and the certified counterexample at $\sigma_\xi = 0.60$ are featured as an *economic
   boundary*: the hump lives where bidder entry is premium-sensitive. Non-monotonicity is the
   identification device (the Corum–Levit 2019, Prop. 4 template), not an embarrassment.

## T5 — The premium wedge (appendix microfoundation)

The disagreement-node tender game delivers $\lambda = 1 - q(1-\gamma)\psi$ in closed form, and
the boundary of the wedge assumption is characterized: $m_1 > m_0$ holds iff not (certain raids
$\wedge$ $\gamma = 0$ $\wedge$ unblockable offers) — all proved. The measured-premium reversal
$M(\pi) = \bar{m}/P$ strictly decreasing in $\pi$ for $\lambda < \lambda_{\mathrm{crit}}$ (fixed
cutoffs) is the object that rationalizes Celentano–Levine's $-13.7\%$ ($-5.2$pp)
activism–premium estimate.

## No-manipulation discipline

Because takeover entry is a corrective action that can make firm value non-monotone in the state
(the EGJ 2015 Case-2 warning), draft_v3 states an explicit sufficient condition under which the
blockholder cannot profitably mislead the bidder — the analog of EGJ's
$R_H - R_L > \tfrac{4x}{3}$ — as a one-remark lemma.

# Empirical Design {#sec-empirics}

**Discipline.** One dated shock, one signed prediction per test; institutional facts as
anchoring, never as "tests" without exogenous variation; announcement CARs are *disclosure price
impact*, never labeled value creation (preempting Ben-David et al., JF 2026).

## Facts section (facts the model must match)

- **F1 (done, committed):** filing-delay compression around the rule change — median delay
  $7.0 \to 5.0$ business days; share filed within 5 business days $35.7\% \to 75.6\%$
  ($n = 300$ SC 13D originals, 2023Q2–Q3 vs 2024Q3–Q4). Extend to the full 2022–2025 universe
  after fixing the 2025 structured-era parser (0.5–1 day).
- **F2:** stake-at-first-13D distribution; target moments: median $6.2\%$, mean $7.68\%$
  (Collin-Dufresne–Fos 2015); bunching just above $5\%$.
- **F3:** announcement CARs pre/post rule (first-pass medians $1.6\% \to 2.6\%$; vet outliers;
  report quantiles, not means).
- **F4 (deferred, 1–3 weeks):** campaign$\to$takeover transition via EDGAR submissions API
  (SC TO-T / DEFM14A / 8-K); benchmarks: Greenwood–Schor's $18.1\%$ within 12 months;
  Boyson et al.'s $70\%$ within 2 years.

## H1 — Attenuation of the liquidity slope (flagship test of T2)

**Hypothesis.** Shortening the accumulation window moves information release from pre-filing
inference to the filing event; the sensitivity of 13D announcement returns to pre-event
liquidity falls after February 5, 2024.

**Specification.**
$$
\mathrm{CAR}_i[-1, +1] \;=\;
\beta_1\, \mathrm{Amihud}_i \;+\;
\beta_2\, (\mathrm{Amihud}_i \times \mathrm{Post}_i) \;+\;
\gamma\, \mathrm{Post}_i \;+\; \delta' X_i \;+\; \mathrm{FE} \;+\; \varepsilon_i,
$$
with T2's prediction
$$
\operatorname{sign}(\beta_2) \;=\; -\operatorname{sign}(\beta_1)
\qquad \text{(attenuation)}.
$$
Also estimated on $\mathrm{CAR}[-10, +1]$ and in quantile regressions (the mean gap is
outlier-driven; medians are the honest summary).

**Sample and data.** All SC 13D originals 2022-01-01 to 2025-12-31 (9,234 parsed; ~65–70% CRSP
match), US common stocks. CARs, Amihud illiquidity
$\mathrm{Amihud}_i = |r_{i,t}| / (P_{i,t} \cdot \mathrm{Vol}_{i,t})$, log-cap, and turnover come
from the on-disk CRSP daily snapshot (2021–2025, 14,092 PERMNOs); events and stakes from the
repo's EDGAR pipeline; filer type via name regex with hand spot-checks; Fama–French factors from
the Ken French library (free) for robustness.

**Confound handling.** (a) Main spec restricts the post window to February–August 2024, before
the 13G deadline change (September 30, 2024); full-sample robustness adds regime dummies for
2024-09-30 and the structured-data mandate (2024-12-18). (b) T+1 settlement dummy (2024-05-28).
(c) Pre window starts 2023 (universal proxy sits inside the earlier pre window). (d) Placebos:
13G filers (untreated by the 13D change before September 2024); non-activist 13D filers;
low-activism-exposure targets.

**Selection honesty.** Filing is a choice; report filer-mix diagnostics pre/post; interpret
$\beta_2$ as a reduced-form information-content change, with an AFS-style selection correction
as robustness, not headline.

## H2 — Run-up to jump shift (the Collin-Dufresne–Fos template)

The 10-to-5-day compression should shift returns from the pre-filing run-up into the filing-day
jump. Define the run-up share
$$
\rho^{\text{run-up}}_i \;=\; \frac{\mathrm{CAR}_i[-10, -2]}{\mathrm{CAR}_i[-10, +1]},
$$
and test $H_2: \mathbb{E}[\rho^{\text{run-up}} \mid \mathrm{Post}] < \mathbb{E}[\rho^{\text{run-up}}
\mid \mathrm{Pre}]$ against the CDF (2015) benchmark of a ~$7\%$ run-up vs ~$3\%$ jump on
2001–2010. CDF's finding that Kyle's $\lambda$, PIN, and Amihud *fall* during accumulation is
the load-bearing institutional fact for the model's architecture: the market learns from the
disclosure event, not from order-flow inference. Run-up windows use parsed event (trigger)
dates.

## H3 — The hump as falsifiable cross-section (second leg, weeks-scale)

For 13D-target deals receiving a bid within 12 months, hand-collect offer prices (SC TO-T /
8-K Item 1.01 / DEFM14A) and compute
$$
\mathrm{Premium}_i \;=\; \frac{P^{\mathrm{offer}}_i}{P^{\mathrm{unaffected}}_i} - 1,
\qquad P^{\mathrm{unaffected}}_i \text{ at } {-42} \text{ trading days (CRSP snapshot)}.
$$
Test the non-monotone prediction across Amihud quintiles $q \in \{1, \dots, 5\}$:
$$
\mathrm{Premium}_i \;=\; \sum_{q=1}^{5} \theta_q\, \mathbf{1}\{i \in q\} \;+\; \delta' X_i
\;+\; \varepsilon_i,
\qquad
H_3:\; \theta_3 > \theta_1 \;\wedge\; \theta_3 > \theta_5
$$
(sign-flip identification — more credible than a monotone claim precisely because it can fail).
Anchors to confront: Massa–Xu (2013, JFQA): $+10\%$ premium per SD of *target* liquidity (public
bidders); Huang–Maharjan–Nanda (2024, JCF): $-4.5$pp per SD of *acquirer minus target* liquidity
difference, stock deals only (cash deals null — the currency-channel falsification);
Albuquerque–Fos–Schroth (2022): $+0.9$pp per SD Amihud level loading on *both* filing types
(pure stock-picking — must be partialled out); Celentano–Levine (2025): mean premium $36.6\%$,
activism interaction $-5.2$pp, as replication targets.

## Calibration moments the model must match

| Moment | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| 13D announcement CAR | $6.34\%$ ($75.2\%$ treatment) | Albuquerque–Fos–Schroth 2022 |
| Run-up vs filing-day jump | $\sim 7\%$ vs $\sim 3\%$ | Collin-Dufresne–Fos 2015 |
| Stake at first 13D | median $6.2\%$, mean $7.68\%$ | Collin-Dufresne–Fos 2015 |
| Pre-announcement accumulation | $54\%$ of block, $8.5\%$ trading profit | Norli–Østergaard–Schindele 2015 |
| Liquidity $\to$ targeting sign | positive ($0.33\% \to 0.73\%$, IV) | Norli–Østergaard–Schindele 2015 |
| Voice$\to$exit mode shift in liquidity | $-6.9$pp on 13D share | Edmans–Fang–Zur 2013 |
| Mean bid premium | $36.6\%$ | Celentano–Levine 2025 |
| Activism $\to$ premium interaction | $-13.7\%$ ($-5.2$pp) | Celentano–Levine 2025 |
| Takeover prob. lift from activism | $+11$pp (12m), $+7.7$pp | Greenwood–Schor 2009; C&L 2025 |
| Campaign costs by stage | \$1.8M / \$2.9M / \$5.9M | Gantchev 2013 |

# Journal Targets and Risks {#sec-targets}

| Target | Fit | Key risk |
|---|---|---|
| **JF / RFS** (primary) | Theory-forward + institutional anchor + one clean shock; matches the Levit–Malenko–Maug / Burkart–Lee taste | R2's GE region theorem must land; the hump must be honestly labeled; differentiate from Celentano–Levine on page 1 |
| **JFE** (alternative) | If the empirical section grows toward 30–35% (premium subsample + transitions) | JFE's activism space is structural-estimation-dominated; the DiD must be bulletproof on bundled confounds |
| JFQA / RAPS (fallback) | Certain fit | — |

**Risk register.** (i) Another team claims the Feb-2024 shock first — mitigate by executing H1/H2
now (~3–4 days of work on disk-resident data). (ii) The R1 counterexample invites "the hump is
fragile" — preempt by featuring the economic boundary. (iii) CAR-critique referees — CARs are
only ever disclosure price impact; premia come from hand-collected offer prices. (iv) "Too many
moving parts" — the three-branch cut and appendix exiles are the answer. (v) Reproducibility:
the Fact-2 execution code must be committed; the gitignored CRSP snapshot must be backed up
off-repo.

**Execution sequence (post-approval).** (1) Owner approves this angle; (2) theory surgery
(three-branch menu, $\tau$ primitive, T2/T3 proofs, cut-list); (3) empirics: parser fix $\to$
Fact-1 universe $\to$ H1/H2 DiD; (4) premium subsample; (5) compile gates (0 errors, 0 undefined
references) plus `make clean && make all`.
